notesStmt.note: This manuscript was likely produced in 1890 or early in 1891.

This title draft is possibly an earlier version of "Old-Age Recitatives" or "An Old Man's Recitatives," titles that Whitman used in 1890 for groups of poems that he submitted, unsuccessfully, for publication in Arena and Scribner's magazines, respectively (see loc.00229 and loc.00230.

Alternatively, this manuscript might represent an early version of the title used for main section of poetry in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891)—a section which Whitman ultimately decided to title, confusingly, "Good-By my Fancy." It also appeared under that title when it was reprinted (as a "second annex") in the 1891–1892 printing of Leaves of Grass.
